title: Audit oracle for prefix-KV reuse regression gating
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: We observed subtle output deltas when prefix/KV cache reuse occurs under model or config changes. Existing tests flag gross regressions but miss low-signal semantic drift that still degrades product quality for downstream apps. This ticket implements an automated "audit oracle" that will compare in-production-like outputs with and without prefix cache reuse for a curated suite of prompts, surface metrics for gating, and integrate the check into CI/rollout pipelines.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Produce a reproducible comparator that runs N=2000 prompt scenarios across target model variants and config toggles (quantization, kernel selection, batch shaping) and returns per-prompt diffs and aggregate metrics.
- Metrics include: token-level edit distance, normalized log-likelihood delta, embedding cosine similarity (text-embedding-ada-... style), per-turn hallucination flags, and a semantic-drift score (weighted combination).
- Define gating thresholds: e.g., median embedding cosine drop > 0.015 or >1% of prompts with semantic-drift > 0.10 triggers costly-rollout-block.
- Generate human-reviewable artifact (CSV + sampled golden responses + diffed tokens) and a single-pass report uploaded to the QA dashboard.
- Integrate as a pre-release gate for model/config changes to hosted and dedicated pools on runtime-1.20.

Design and approach:
1) Dataset: assemble a "cache-sensitivity corpus" mixing (a) high-reuse developer prompts (docs completion, code continuation, conversational context) (b) P0 production calls sampled from anonymized telemetry (opt-out sanitized) and (c) adversarial synthetic cases that stress KV reuse.
2) Execution harness: a two-arm replay: (A) normal runtime (with prefix/KV reuse enabled) vs (B) bypassed-reuse execution (same model weights/config but forcing cold KV semantics). Both runs should use identical RNG seeds and temperature to isolate cache-induced differences. Record full token-level traces and per-token logprobs.
3) Metrics and scoring: compute per-example artifacts and aggregate statistics. Build a drift scorer that penalizes semantically meaningful changes more than safe punctuation/tokenization shifts.
4) Sampling and cost control: run full N job in CI for major rollouts; run a fast smoke (N=250) for patch changes. Provide an incremental mode that reuses cached comparisons when unrelated layers/configs change.
5) Automation: add a GH Actions job and a runtime release hook that triggers the audit on model or inference-config changes. Results should produce a gating verdict (pass/warn/fail) and link to the report.

Integration points and artifacts:
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/prefix-kv-audit (draft)
- Draft PR for harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1829 (WIP)
- QA dashboard destination: https://console.redwood.ai/qa/audit-results/kv-prefix

Risks and mitigations:
- Flakiness from non-deterministic kernels: mitigate by pinning kernels where possible and by running multi-seed averages.
- Cost of large replays: mitigate via stratified sampling and fast-smoke gates.
- False-positive gating for trivial tokenization changes: tune drift scorer with human-labeled calibration set and add a secondary review bucket.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (this ticket): implement harness, internal run on staging corpus, produce report for runtime-1.20 branch (ETA 2026-03-24).
- Phase 2: automate GH/CI hook and warning-level alerts for dedicated capacity changes (ETA 2026-04-07).
- Phase 3: enforce hard gate for hosted major model changes after 2-week observation window (ETA 2026-04-21).

Acceptance tests:
- Demo run comparing v1 -> v1+config showing no gated regression on smoke corpus.
- Injected regression test where we intentionally modify cache indexing behavior should fail the gate and surface actionable diffs.
